captions.text: Recap of chapter 23: some questions need two facts, such as a band and the rule for that band.
The agent could search twice, and it almost never did, whatever we told it.
So Split asked for the facts first, and code ran every search.
Both files came back in about half the runs. There's still a gap to look at.
Today's black box: a plan, carried out one step at a time.
Let's open it. But first, the question that still fails.
A shift lead's notice needs pay-bands.md and resignation.md. Predict: how many runs see both?
The agent searches once, finds the rule, and lists the bands. Three runs, the same each time.
Split searches three times, and gives three answers: 2 weeks, 4 weeks and 8 weeks.
Only the run that saw pay-bands.md was right. The other two picked a band.
Split wrote every search before it read anything. Try it by hand: search, read, then search again.
The first search finds pay-bands.md. Shift lead: Band C.
Now you can write Band C in the next search. The question never said that.
That's the new idea: a later search can use what an earlier step found.
First, the model writes a plan: the facts to look up, in order, at most three.
Ask for two plans, and search for nothing. Predict: will the first plan say to find the band?
No. It's tidy, and it would fit almost any question about any handbook.
Your code owns the loop. Every step runs, so the model can't stop after one search.
Each later search is written from the step and everything known so far. Split can't do this.
Then the model writes one note on what the search found, and the note joins what's known.

captions.text: Run it. The first note kept one band: Band E. Later searches went looking for Band E.
One of them happened to bring back pay-bands.md, and the answer was right. No step asked for it.

scenes.start: for step, query, note in zip

captions.text: The next run had the same wrong note, missed that file, and said 8 weeks.
We ran it four times, and it was right once. One run proves little, so measure.

scenes.start: for name, _, question, answers, files in HOPS

captions.text: Four setups, six hop questions, ten runs each. Step by step has notes, and no plan.
Earned means right, and the searches saw both files. So the answer could have come from the facts.
Plan makes 7 calls and Split makes 2. Predict: how much better is Plan?
It isn't. 20 and 20 strict, 14 and 16 earned. That's too close to rank, at 3.5 times the calls.
Setups that left searching to the model searched about once, and earned nothing.
Each earned pass cost Split 7.5 calls, and Plan 30.
Question by question. The repair questions need only one file, so earned is too harsh there.
On those, the plain agent is best: 18 of 20, at 2 calls. Plan gets 9.
Where both files are needed, Plan earned 8 and Split 6, of 40. That can't be ranked either.
Did good plans do it? Three questions turn on a band. None of the 30 plans says band.
They earned 8 anyway. And 7 Harbour plans name the arrival time, and earned none.
Read them yourself. These three earned, and none names the band or says why it's looking.
So the gain may come from more searching, not smarter planning. Split searched 2.8 times, with no plan.
This test can't separate them. Exercise 6 tries three generic searches with no plan.
What still fails? harbour-arrive: 0 of 10. It finds the opening time, and stops.
No run saw shifts.md. Adding Harbour to the query pulled the search towards Harbour's logs.
senior-beans: no earned passes. Only 2 of 10 saw pay-bands.md, and no step asked for it.
So a plan can drop what mattered. The search only knows the step, and that's the model's rewording.

scenes.start: for name, kind, question, answers, _ in CONTROLS

captions.text: The control: 8 direct and 4 unanswerable questions. Predict: does a longer process invent answers?
No. All four scored 36 of 36. Plan did no harm, and paid 7 calls for what 2 calls got.
We tested one 7B model on six questions. A bigger model may plan better, so measure yours.

captions.text: Plan writes the steps, code runs every one, and each search can use what came before.
On this test it tied Split, and forcing the searches mattered more than the plan.
So measure the searches, the files and the cost, and read the plans.
